summary: East Butte: Deschutes NF L-4 lookout; 1932 original on a 30-ft tower, 1995-96 replacement on a 20-ft tower; active, staffed in summer; gated road access.

facts.design: L-4 gable-roof cab on a wooden tower

access.note: Gated road at NF-750 with about 1.7 miles of road walking to the summit; the nearby OHV trail system closes June 1 to October 1. A 2023 trip report says visitors are not invited up to the cab; its writers had read this was because of heavy traffic from people and ATVs. That is one visitor's account, not an official access rule.

visit.trail_note: Park at the gate on NF-750 and walk about 1.7 miles of road to the summit, or take the ATV trail. The OHV trail up the butte is closed June 1 to October 1.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Deschutes National Forest, Bend-Fort Rock Ranger District)

events.note: Emergency lookout stationed on the butte in August
First lookout, an L-4 on a 30-foot wooden tower; firelookout.com says fire detection began that year and a 1992 Bulletin item says it was built in 1932
Local history site describes a 14x14 gable-roof lookout cabin constructed on a 30-foot round timber tower
Standard plan T-1E wood-frame garage built at the lookout site
Lookout Sylvia Andrews relayed messages to and from the Aspen Flat fire and received a $100 award
Inspection found the tower and cab had deteriorated and posed safety risks
Forest Service asked for comments on a plan to replace the tower and cabin, or to restore and relocate the existing structure
Lookout duties moved to Fox Butte; in the spring the old tower was cut down and the cabin burned
New L-4 gable-roof cab on a 20-foot wooden tower, which the NHLR dates to 1995
Weebly history says the new tower was finished and duties were returned from Fox Butte; conflicts with the NHLR 1995 build year
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on March 1, 2003
Cheryl Hill visit on June 11, 2021 found the tower staffed
Trip report on May 14, 2023 lists the lookout as active and currently standing

corrections.why: 9.1 m is 30 feet, the height of the original 1932-era tower. The current L-4 cab stands on a 20-foot wooden tower per the NHLR and Cheryl Hill's '20 L-4 tower' listing.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR gives 6,371 ft (1,942 m), which matches the brief's record, while firelookout.com and Cheryl Hill give 6,400 ft. Not resolved here. The brief value is kept and both figures are reported in the story.
The NHLR and the Weebly index place the lookout in Deschutes County; firelookout.com says Lake County. Deschutes is kept, matching the forest and the Bend-Fort Rock district.

resolved_conflicts.field: build year of the current structure
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR dates the replacement to 1995, while the Weebly history says construction began in 1995 and the tower was finished in 1996. Both are reported.
firelookout.com and a 1992 Bulletin item say 1932; a 1933 entry describes a 14x14 cabin built on a 30-foot tower. Both are reported.

notes_for_editor: Original 1932 tower and 1995-96 replacement are well documented across sources; the NHLR says 1995 and the Weebly history says 1996 for the finished tower. Elevation (6,371 vs 6,400 ft) and county (Deschutes vs Lake) conflict and are not resolved. The brief height_m 9.1 is the original 30-ft tower, corrected to 6.1 for the current 20-ft tower. The 1959 fire item is from a Bend Bulletin article quoted by the Weebly site. The 2023 'not invited up' remark is one visitor's account and is not an official access rule. The Roaming Civic 2023 title and date come from a search result; the quoted lines were fetched from its page. firelookout.com says the 1995 structure is a replica of the original 30-foot tower, while the NHLR and Cheryl Hill say 20 feet. The record uses 20 feet (6.1 m) and the story attributes the 20-foot figure to the NHLR. This conflict is not in the story.
